incident-bot: INCIDENT SEV=3 · region=us-west-2 · GPUs saturated, autoscaler failing, spot interruptions causing insufficient fallback capacity. Paging: @Alex J (oncall).

incident-bot: symptoms: hosted/generate and hosted/chat latency spike, 5xxs rising, request queue depth 1.2k -> 4.5k in 18m. Autoscaler status: erroring when requesting new preemptible instances; fallback pools near 95% utilized. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/infr/alerts/2811112222

Alex J: oncall here — seeing queue explosion. Jumping into autoscaler logs now. Can someone post recent cloud provider errors?

Sara I: past 25m see mix of `InsufficientCapacity` and `QuotaExceeded` when autoscaler called provider API. Looks like spot pool had a simultaneous preempt batch. Snippet from autoscaler: 

```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z ERROR autoscaler.go:431 call_provider: request failure: InsufficientCapacity: NotEnoughInstances
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z WARN autoscaler.go:439 backoff 30s -> 60s
2026-03-15T02:12:03Z ERROR autoscaler.go:431 call_provider: request failure: QuotaExceeded: Customer request exceeds quota for GPU-v100
```

Sara I: provider also returned transient 429s on their quota endpoint, which caused parallel requests to pile up.

Mike R: runtime note — queue growth is amplified because KV cache hit-rate dropped on many hosts after preemptions. Cold cache increases token work by ~25% per request, so autoscaler sees higher CPU/GPU utilization and tries to scale more, making the loop worse.

Alex J: good catch. For immediate mitigation I'm going to: 1) lower max_concurrency on hosted/generate to 1 (reduce in-flight tokens per GPU), 2) enable route-level degradation to the small-model fallback (gpt-small-quant) for non-SLAs, 3) pause batcher aggregation (to reduce tail latency). Doing step 1 now.

Alex J: `apictl route update hosted/generate --concurrency 1` -> rolled, telemetry shows slight drop in GPU utilization but queue still rising due to inflight backlog.

Kate C: CS — which customers are in the error tail? I'm getting pings from two mid-market customers complaining about 503s. List of impacted org ids?

Mike R: partial list from trace sampling: org_112, org_479, org_884 (high-qps). We should proactively message org_112 and org_479. SLA exposure: possible 5-15min request failures depending on backlog position.

Sara I: trying immediate capacity option — requesting on-demand (non-spot) GPUs in us-west-2 as emergency. Cloud request command queued; provider throttled our quota calls but one request got accepted: `request-id=od-7f3b`. Starting provisioning watch.

infra-bot: Cloud event: request-id=od-7f3b status=provisioning ETA ~7m.

Alex J: also opening cross-region failover to us-west-1 for low-priority traffic. Command: `rctl route-shift --service hosted/generate --percent 15 --to us-west-1` — shifting 15% now.

Mike R: also toggling KV cache warmth strategy — forcing cache priming on newly provisioned nodes to reduce cold miss storm. Patch posted to runtime: `hot-prime` flag on pool creation.

Sara I: cloud update: request-id=od-7f3b status=active at 2026-03-15T02:25:40Z. Added 8 on-demand GPUs to fallback pool. Monitoring ramp.

Alex J: queue depth stabilized at ~2.6k and 5xxs trending down from 12% -> 4% since on-demand added and concurrency reduced. Still degraded. We'll keep mitigation until queue <500 and 5xx <1%.

Kate C: sending templated notice to impacted customers: "We're experiencing degraded inference capacity in us-west-2 due to cloud spot reclaim activity. We've enabled temporary fallbacks and added on-demand capacity. We're monitoring and will update in 15 minutes." Sending now.

Mike R: recommended follow-ups: - tune autoscaler backoff jitter to avoid synchronized retries, - add emergency on-demand reserve for critical tenants, - improve KV cache priming for preempt events.

Alex J: agree. Also we'll add a short-term runbook change: on spot wave, immediately try 1) request small on-demand block, 2) reduce concurrency globally, 3) route non-critical traffic off-region, 4) start customer comms. I'll open a post-incident task.

Ryan N: I'm next oncall in ~20m. Alex, please handoff once we reach stable state. If you need me earlier ping.

Alex J: handoff plan: will watch for 30m. Current state snapshot: queue=2.3k, 5xx=3.6%, fallback pool utilization=88%, on-demand added=8 GPUs (active). Actions taken: concurrency throttled, batcher paused, route shift 15%, cache priming, emergency on-demand. Investigations to continue: provider quota flakiness and autoscaler retry logic.

Alex J: handing off at 2811113822 -> Ryan N. If anything spikes above queue>3.5k or 5xx>8% escalate to SEV2 and DM SRE lead.

Ryan N: taking it. Saved playbook. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate with infra for capacity requests.

Sara I: follow-up note: provider support ticket opened `SUP-99821` re: quota anomalies. Also attaching autoscaler logs for postmortem.

Mike R: quick risk note — the reduce-concurrency change may increase tail latency for single-user heavy requests; we'll track p95/p99. Set alert on p99>30s.

Kate C: CS update: customers notified. One escalation opened by org_479 support: PM asked for ETA. I'm saying 30m to full recovery but keeping them updated.

Alex J: wrapping up — will file postmortem draft and proposed fixes (autoscaler backoff, on-demand reserve, cache priming patch). Handoff complete.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: moved to monitoring. severity downgraded to SEV4.
